ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10616, as amended), its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 33179), the Financial Services Commission Regulation on Customer Due Diligence and Reporting, the Commercial Act (Act No. 16912), the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 18176), and the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5493, as amended). Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) has examination access to UBO/CDD records, and the National Tax Service and Financial Supervisory Service exercise parallel supervisory powers over high-risk wholesale activities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Corporate Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Commercial Registration Division / Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Korean notary public followed by issuance of a Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the receiving state is an Apostille Convention member; for non-member states, notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate in the receiving state. These two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korea: consolidated Certificate of Company Registration Facts, Business Registration Certificate, and National Tax Service Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service and District Court Commercial Registration Division
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a Korean notary public followed by Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention destinations; for non-Apostille states, notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean consular post of the destination country. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, mutually exclusive procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney Authorizing Formation, Regulatory Filing, and Bank Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding members and designated managing member of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution, notarization, and then either Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consular legalization at the competent Korean embassy/consulate; the chosen method depends exclusively on whether the recipient state is an Apostille Convention member, and both methods are never used sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Certified True Copy Certified by Notary and Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and District Court registration office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille if the destination state is party to the Apostille Convention; if the destination state is non-party, consular legalization at the destination's Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Commercial Relationship and Transaction Conduct Statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate banking institution in Korea maintaining the applicant's or parent's trade finance and cash-management accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of signatory capacity where applicable followed by Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention countries; for non-member states, consular legalization through the Korean ministry of foreign affairs and the receiving state's consulate, never combining the two legalization mechanisms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Pharmaceutical Wholesale License Eligibility and UBO Declaration Package
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and local municipal health authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and either Hague Apostille or consular legalization according to the destination jurisdiction's convention status; the path is singular and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All founders, directors, managers, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, ultimate shareholders, and material counterparties must be screened continuously against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions lists, UK HM Treasury, EU consolidated sanctions, and the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Financial Services Commission sanctions notices. Politically exposed person (PEP) identification must follow FATF Recommendation 12 and Korean FSC customer due diligence rules, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must occur at pre-incorporation, before account opening, before opening documentary letters of credit, and on an ongoing transaction-monitoring basis, with adverse media review and beneficial ownership verification documented for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr and the Commercial Registry Information Network of the National Court Administration; name reservation applications are processed through the electronic registration system of the competent district court.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Korean company name must be written in Hangul. The statutory name follows the four-tier convention: (1) distinctive trade/brand token, (2) objective or business-purpose descriptor, (3) optional geographic locator, and (4) mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa or LLC. Latin-alphabet names may be registered as secondary trade names only and cannot replace the required Hangul name; foreign words must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul for registration purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation under Korean commercial law is valid for 180 days and is not statutorily extendable; if more time is needed, a new reservation application must be filed after the original reservation lapses. If the district court registrar rejects the proposed name for similarity, misleading indication, or a prohibited token, counsel may request a written rejection notice and file a written objection with the registrar within 14 days. If the objection is denied, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Seoul Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act. For pharmaceutical-related tokens, prior written approval from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety should be obtained and attached to the re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale Yuhan Hoesa. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, National Tax Service, and commercial banks reject a virtual address because the business requires a physical place of business, temperature-controlled and GSP/GDP-compliant storage, a qualified pharmaceutical manager, and verifiable operational substance. A virtual address may be used only for temporary pre-incorporation correspondence and never for VAT registration, pharmaceutical licensing, or corporate banking; reliance on a virtual office will cause license refusal, business registration cancellation, and increased AML risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) signed lease for a physical office and warehouse; (2) corporate signage physically present; (3) qualified pharmaceutical manager on site; (4) GSP/GDP-compliant storage and temperature logs; (5) electronic tax invoices and VAT records tied to the physical address; (6) bank statements and account opening files matching the registered office; (7) registered office answerable during business hours. Quantified risk: 90% probability of an unannounced MFDS or municipal tax inspection within the first 12 months, 75% probability of a joint National Tax Service and pharmaceutical-affairs physical inspection before initial license approval, and 50% probability of a bank site visit before account opening for API cross-border customers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, especially Articles 543 through 589 governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), including Articles 553, 554, 555, 560, 563, 584, 586 and 600; Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, Articles 44 and 45 for wholesale drug licensing; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Articles 6 and 14 for non-resident investments and cross-border trade settlements when applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Dung-gi-so) having jurisdiction over the Republic of Korea registered office address; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (I-RO) is accepted for provisional submissions and final registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit, first board resolution minutes, consent letters of directors and auditor, and proof of registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. There is no blocked escrow account requirement under Korean law; however, before the registry will accept the incorporation filing, the full amount of the capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be deposited with a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea and confirmed by a Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit. For foreign-invested capital exceeding KRW 100 million, the investor must file a foreign investment report with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or its designated receival agency, and any foreign exchange transaction must be made through a bank authorized for foreign exchange business.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
WHEREAS, the initial members and subscribers of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), having executed the Articles of Incorporation, desire to organize and incorporate the Company as a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea;
WHEREAS, all issued membership interests have been duly subscribed, and the required paid-in capital has been fully paid and deposited with a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea, as evidenced by the Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit;
WHEREAS, the Company has selected a physical registered office within the Republic of Korea as required for corporate registration and administrative notices;
WHEREAS, the execution of the Company's statutory banking arrangements, opening of corporate accounts, and appointment of officers are necessary for lawful trade in pharmaceutical active pharmaceutical ingredients, and the Company desires to authorize such transactions and appointments.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the unanimous consent of the initial members, directors, and subscribers of the Company, as follows:
1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The capital subscription as disclosed in the Articles of Incorporation is hereby ratified and confirmed, including authorized membership interests, issuable proportions, and fully paid contributions by the initial members. The representative director is instructed to issue capital contribution receipts and maintain statutory capital records.
2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board designates the bank named in the Company's banking questionnaire as the principal depository and payment institution. The representative director, together with any two designated signatories where required, is authorized to open check, demand deposit, foreign currency, and correspondent banking accounts; to execute account resolutions; to arrange SWIFT wire transfers, electronic bank transfers, documentary credits, and trade finance lines incident to the Company's wholesale API import and export operations; and to maintain internet banking credentials subject to corporate controls.
3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office be and hereby is fixed at the address recorded in the Articles of Incorporation, Republic of Korea. The representative director is directed to retain the office and warehouse lease, to notify taxation authorities, and to maintain the registered office at all times.
4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The person named in the appointment schedule is hereby appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer with authority to manage the Company's ordinary business; the person named as director is hereby appointed as Director; the person named as auditor is hereby appointed as Auditor if required under the Company's Articles of Incorporation; and the person named as compliance officer is hereby appointed as Compliance Officer for regulated affairs. All officers shall have full authority to bind the Company within the scope of ordinary business and to sign all statutory filings, tax returns, and regulatory submissions.
5. INCORPORATION, FILING AND LICENSING AUTHORIZATION: The Representative Director and Compliance Officer are authorized jointly and severally to prepare, execute, notarize, file and prosecute the incorporation registration before the District Court Registry Office, the business registration before the National Tax Service, and the pharmaceutical wholesale dealer license application before the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. They are authorized to engage professional advisers, incur registration fees and license fees, and execute all ancillary documents.
6. GENERAL EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution is effective immediately and shall continue in full force until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the members. The minutes shall be signed by the chair and recorded in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Articles of Incorporation Drafting, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registry Information Service (I-RO) for name search; Korean Notary Public for notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search using the Supreme Court Registration Office's Internet Registration System to secure a unique Korean-name reservation. Draft the Articles of Incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa, stating the corporate purpose as wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients and any other lawful business. The purpose clause must be broad enough to match the later Pharmaceutical Wholesale Dealer License under Article 44 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. Execute and notarize the Articles before a Korean notary, ensuring that each initial member's contribution, valuation, and payment method are recorded. The notary will issue a notarized copy suitable for submission to the registry, and the draft should include the capital schedule, duration, registered office address, and identities of directors and auditor.
required_dossiers: Passport or government-issued ID of each initial member
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
Registered office lease or address consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to a conflicting Korean corporate name, select an alternative name and submit a new reservation. If the notary issues a corrective request because the purpose clause is insufficiently specific to pharmaceutical wholesale, amend the purpose clause and re-notarize the Articles before proceeding to capital deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a Temporary Bank Account and Deposit of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank authorized to issue the Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit under the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of the company or its subscribers at a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea. Deposit the full amount of the initial capital before filing the incorporation registration. The bank will issue a Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit stating the account holder, deposit date, and amount. This certificate is a mandatory registry element proving that capital contributions have actually been made. If any non-resident contributes capital, the account opening must comply with foreign exchange transaction rules and, when the investment exceeds KRW 100 million, the investor must file or obtain a foreign investment report receipt. The banking officer will complete KYC checks and may require a description of the company's intended pharmaceutical API trade and ultimate beneficial owner information.
required_dossiers: Passports or government-issued IDs of contributing members
Foreign investment report return receipt, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires an additional corporate identifier before the company is registered, provide a notarized declaration and the preliminary foreign investment filing. If the application is suspended due to sanctions screening or incomplete KYC, correct the beneficial ownership information and resubmit; if the bank refuses the account, open the temporary deposit account with another licensed commercial bank and reissue the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation at the Local District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the registered office address; online via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation under Article 600 of the Commercial Act after the capital certificate has been issued. The application must contain the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit, the first board resolution minutes, written acceptances from the directors and auditor, consent of the representative director, and proof of the registered office location. Pay the prescribed registration and education fees. The registry examiner will verify the legal form, capital contribution, and adequacy of the submitted documents. Upon approval, the court issues a certified certificate of registration, and the Yuhan Hoesa legally exists as a separate limited liability entity. The filing should be completed within 20 days of the notarial execution and capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board resolution
Consent letters to serve as director and auditor
Office lease or proof of registered office
Identity documents of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a corrective order, supply the requested certified documents within the prescribed period, normally 14 days. If the registration is rejected, prepare a clean resubmission with the missing items and pay the re-filing fee; repeated rejection should be resolved through a professional attorney, and an administrative remedy may be sought through the court registry's supervisory review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service; online through HomeTax (Hometax.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days from the date of incorporation registration, apply for a Business Registration Certificate. File through the HomeTax portal, selecting the income type as corporation and the business classification code corresponding to wholesale distribution of pharmaceutical products, aligned with ISIC 4649. Upload the certified certificate of incorporation registration, identity documents, lease contract, bank account confirmation, and Articles of Incorporation. The National Tax Service will issue the business registration certificate, which enables the company to issue statutory tax invoices, file VAT returns, and comply with corporate tax obligations. This certificate is also a precondition for the Pharmaceutical Wholesale Dealer License, and the tax office may ask for a physical inspection of the office before issuance.
required_dossiers: Registered office ownership or lease proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests supplementary documentation or a site inspection, respond within 10 days with the requested leases, floor plans, and identity documents. If the business registration certificate is delayed or denied because of an incomplete address, correct the address and file an amendment; an administrative appeal is available before the Tax Tribunal if the denial is unlawful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pharmaceutical Wholesale Dealer License Application and Facility Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), regional office with jurisdiction over the principal place of business, or the delegated mayor/governor/district licensing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business Registration Certificate, apply for the Pharmaceutical Wholesale Dealer License under Article 44 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. The application must show compliance with facility requirements, including secure storage areas, temperature control for APIs as needed, locked cabinets for controlled substances if applicable, and the employment of a responsible pharmacist or qualified specialist. Submit floor plans, proof of lease, business registration certificate, Articles of Incorporation, responsible pharmacist employment consent, and quality management standard operating procedures. The licensing authority will inspect the premises and verify storage conditions, segregation of products, cold-chain capability, and record-keeping systems. The license is issued only after a successful facility inspection, and any change of location or responsible pharmacist requires a fresh license or amendment.
required_dossiers: Application form for pharmaceutical wholesale dealer license
Floor plan of warehouse and office
Lease contract for the licensed premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MFDS issues a supplementation request, submit all required corrections within the stated period, normally 10 to 15 days. If the license is denied, the company may file an administrative appeal with the Central Administrative Appeals Commission and subsequently an administrative lawsuit with the Seoul Administrative Court. Temporary closure orders may be cured by remedying inventory segregation, temperature monitoring, or pharmacist staffing deficiencies and applying for reinstatement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) for pharmaceutical wholesale licensing; Ministry of Environment for environmental matters; local fire and construction authorities for physical premises; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Pharmaceutical Wholesale Dealer License under Article 44 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act of the Republic of Korea

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MoE) and the local Si/Gun/Gu environmental regulator; Korea Environment Corporation for delegated technical review
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for the stated wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients, as no pharmaceutical manufacturing, chemical synthesis, assembly, or treatment operation is conducted. If the company installs cold storage or warehousing with a total floor area exceeding the local EIA screening threshold, or discharges wastewater exceeding 50 cubic meters per day, an environmental examination may be required before site construction or expansion.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharge is expected from ordinary wholesale office and warehouse operations. Sanitary wastewater must meet municipal sewerage standards under the Sewerage Act. If a diesel emergency generator is installed, diesel fuel storage above 1,000 liters requires a petroleum storage registration, and exhaust emissions must conform to the Air Conservation Act. Any hazardous pharmaceutical waste or expired API disposed of must be manifested and transported under the Wastes Control Act, and the company must retain waste shipment records for at least 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The warehouse and office must obtain a Fire Safety Completion Inspection under the Fire Suppression and Fire-Fighting Facility Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Management Act, including certification of fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, emergency exits, and sprinkler systems where required by building area and racking height. A structural loading clearance is required if the warehouse uses high-density pallet racking. The company must also obtain a workplace safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act from the Ministry of Employment and Labor, covering chemical substance safety data sheets, personal protective equipment, emergency response plans, and worker training before commencing API handling operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Customs administration is vested in the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity with no domestic place of business must appoint a domestic tax representative under Article 109 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and file a business registration application with the jurisdictional district tax office via HomeTax. Required supporting documents include: (i) executed power of attorney to the domestic tax representative, (ii) a certified copy of the foreign company charter or articles of incorporation and foreign business registration certificate, (iii) proof of foreign tax residency, (iv) evidence of a Korean fixed place of business (e.g., lease agreement or branch address registration), and (v) identity documents of the tax representative and ultimate beneficial owner. The NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate (Saeupja Deungrokjeung) containing the ten-digit business registration number, which serves simultaneously as the corporate tax identification number and the VAT registration number. Foreign entities deriving only royalty, service, or dividend income without a domestic fixed place normally do not require business registration and instead are subject to simplified withholding tax procedures; however, any import-then-export wholesale operation involving physical inventory in Korea mandates business registration before customs clearance. Applications are screened against the Korea Customs Service and local licensing requirements; for a pharmaceutical API wholesale entity, submission of the statutory pharmaceutical wholesaler license is additionally required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Korean Corporate Tax Act does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch classification elections. A Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation with entity-level taxation and is not pass-through eligible.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) as imposed under the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 10,000,000 (aproximately USD 8,000) of taxable turnover in the preceding calendar year; a new business engaging in taxable supplies must apply for VAT business registration within 20 days from the date operations commence. Where a foreign entity lacks a domestic place of business, VAT registration is required through a tax representative if it makes a taxable supply from a Korean fixed establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices for business-to-business supplies must be issued as electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system or a certified ERP integration application programming interface. The e-tax invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS at the time of issuance, implementing near-real-time fiscal reporting. No separate manual clearance stamp or physical anti-fraud fiscal marking is required; however, each e-tax invoice carries a unique NTS-issued electronic invoice number, and the two fiscal reporting cycles for VAT returns (half-yearly, with interim filings) are mandatory. Failure to transmit e-tax invoices on time or incorrect data submission exposes the taxpayer to penalty tax under Article 32 of the Value-Added Tax Act, ranging from 1% to 3% of the invoice value depending on the violation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 22(1) of the Value-Added Tax Act, zero-rated VAT applies to exported goods and qualified services supplied to non-residents. For a pharmaceutical API wholesale exporter, the statutory criteria are: (i) the goods must be physically moved out of South Korea and delivered overseas under a customs export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, (ii) the exporter must hold a definitive foreign exchange payment evidence recognized by a licensed Korean bank, and (iii) the export declaration number must be reconciled with the VAT return. The supply becomes zero-rated at the time the export is declared, irrespective of the sale price; however, input VAT incurred on purchase of locally sourced APIs or business expenses is creditable, and any excess input VAT after the zero-rated sales is refundable under the accelerated export refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Export Entry) accepted by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, bearing the export declaration number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the physical conveyance of goods outside South Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued export proceeds certificate demonstrating receipt of payment in foreign currency
Commercial Invoice in English or Korean describing the pharmaceutical APIs and their H.S. classification
Statutory pharmaceutical wholesale export approval/license and any certificate of analysis required by the destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS cross-matches each zero-rated VAT return against the Korea Customs Service export declaration database and bank foreign exchange receipt records. If zero-rating is claimed without a valid export declaration, or without the goods having actually left Korean customs territory, the NTS will recharacterize the supply as a domestic taxable supply, levy the standard 10% VAT, and impose penalty tax: (i) 20% of the relevant tax amount for negligent understatement under the Framework Act on National Taxes, (ii) 40% for fraudulent or egregious misstatement, plus statutory interest computed on a daily basis from the original return due date. Export proceeds not repatriated within the 540-day statutory settlement period under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act are separately subject to KCS administrative fines and may trigger cancellation of the export declaration, with retrospective VAT clawback and penalties. Where patterns of fabricated export declarations or forged FIRCs are detected, the case is referred to the Supreme Prosecutors' Office for tax evasion fraud with potential imprisonment of up to five years, fines up to KRW 100,000,000, and additional punitive charges under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, and for most capital account transactions, subject to reporting and declaration requirements under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds; exporters may hold foreign currency in domestic foreign currency accounts or overseas accounts, but must repatriate proceeds within a statutory period (generally one year from the export date, with extensions possible on application). Profit remittance for foreign investors, including dividends, is permitted after settlement of corporate tax liabilities and is subject to a 20% withholding tax (or treaty-reduced rate), with supporting documents such as audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, board minutes for dividend declaration, and a remittance purpose report. For capital account transactions, such as foreign direct investment (FDI) capital injection and loans, prior declaration or registration is required with the Bank of Korea via a foreign exchange bank, but there is no general licensing bottleneck. Cross-border payments must be routed through authorized foreign exchange banks; use of virtual assets or crypto-assets is strictly regulated. South Korea does not impose a dual-rate system or currency controls that prevent full convertibility; rather, the regime relies on transaction transparency, reporting thresholds, and AML/KYC compliance. A pharmaceutical API wholesale entity will require typical trade finance documentation, including invoices and transport documents, to support the underlying transaction and avoid anti-money-laundering scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory conversion into KRW. Exporters must repatriate foreign currency receipts within one year from the date of exportation (the 'collection period') unless an extension is granted by a foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, and funds may be held in Foreign Exchange Accounts, Foreign Exchange Settlement Accounts, or overseas accounts. However, the export letter of credit, bill of exchange, or shipping documents must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank within 15 days of export approval, and actual settlement must be completed through an authorized bank to demonstrate compliance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Verification Escrow Account for initial foreign direct investment capital
Basic Operational KRW Current Account with foreign currency sub-account
Corporate Current Account and Export Proceeds Receivable Account
Trade Finance Settlement Account supporting LC issuance and SWIFT MT103 operations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. South Korean law under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree restricts foreign exchange business to authorized foreign exchange banks. Fintech EMIs such as Payoneer, Wise, and Airwallex do not hold a Korean foreign exchange bank license and are legally barred from directly offering foreign exchange settlement or proprietary cross-border clearing to Korean entities. They can only operate as payment facilitators or technology providers in partnership with licensed domestic banks, under the bank's compliance and reporting framework. For a high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale entity requiring LC and comprehensive bank confirmation, relying on a fintech EMI without direct Korean settlement rails is not viable; the statutory corporate banking relationship must be with a licensed tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For South Korean corporate account onboarding, the statutory director or a designated authorized signatory must physically appear at a domestic branch for identity verification and signature specimen registration. Remote account opening without physical presence is not generally permitted under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and current AML regulations. For non-resident directors, a physical visit is mandatory unless the bank's compliance committee approves an exceptional consular confirmation procedure, which requires apostilled power of attorney, certified passport copies, and video-interview validation. Given the high-risk pharmaceutical API trade classification, the bank will require a face-to-face interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and the individual holding management control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical API wholesale is classified under anti-money-laundering high-risk standards due to dual-use chemical precursors and potential diversion to unlicensed producers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide valid pharmaceutical wholesale license issued by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), a detailed product catalog with HS codes and CAS numbers, proof of compliance with narcotics and psychotropic substance control permits (if applicable), and an internal compliance policy addressing restricted party screening and end-use verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership structure of the Korean LLC with foreign shareholders, triggering enhanced beneficial ownership disclosure requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the LLC's Certificate of Registry (Business Registration Certificate), a notarized and apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation from the parent jurisdiction, an updated ownership chain chart identifying all natural persons with 25% or more ownership, and certified passport copies of UBOs and directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident affiliate may be scrutinized as potential money laundering or an unregistered foreign exchange transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the equity subscription agreement or loan agreement, board resolutions approving the capital transaction, source-of-funds evidence (six months of bank statements and audited financial statements of the sending entity), and a completed Foreign Exchange Declaration Form filed with the Bank of Korea through the receiving bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade sanctions screening flags on consignees in sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions, especially concerning pharmaceutical ingredients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a notarized end-user certificate, an end-use statement attested by the customer, the full set of transport and commercial documents (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading), and a systemic sanctions-report demonstrating negative screening against OFAC-EU-UN lists, transactional screening logs, and a PDF copy of the bank's denial-of-export confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound capital injection by a foreign shareholder into the Korean LLC, the compliant routing is as follows: (1) the non-resident investor opens a Foreign-investment Registration via the investee company's central bank designated foreign exchange bank, submitting an application for registration with the Bank of Korea. (2) The remittance is executed via SWIFT MT103 including a purpose of payment/code such as 'Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Subscription' or 'Capital Increase', referencing the registered investment number. (3) The receiving bank credits a temporary capital escrow account or a Foreign Exchange Purchase Account, and after receiving the wire, the bank issues a Certificate of Acceptance of Foreign Investment and completes a cap verification exchange transaction. (4) The capital is transferred to the LLC's operating account only after submission of the Certificate of Receipt of Foreign Investment, proof of business registration, and a settlement disclosure form to the Tax Office. (5) For foreign exchange affairs, a 'Report of Payment for Foreign Debt' may also be required if the injection is structured as shareholder loan. The entire process must be completed within the statutory reporting window to avoid administrative penalties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for API purchases shall be processed through the following clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 remittance for open-account settlements, requiring a commercial invoice, purchase order, bill of lading, and a foreign exchange declaration form specifying the trade purpose code. (b) Commercial Letters of Credit issued by the Korean bank to the seller's bank via SWIFT MT700, with subsequent MT710/MT720/MT750 amendments and MT202/MT202COV for cover payments, using the underlying LC terms. (c) Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) under SWIFT MT400/MT410/MT700, with the bank acting as collecting agent. All outbound disbursements must be settled through the authorized foreign exchange bank, and payments exceeding USD 5,000 require the submission of supporting trade documents. For high-risk pharma transactions, an additional Product Compliance Certificate (free sale certificate) and Certificate of Analysis must be attached.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards on KRW/USD with a maximum tenor of 1 year, directly linked to forecast export receipts or import payables; prior bank approval is required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for cross-currency exposures where onshore KRW delivery is not desired, provided the underlying trade transaction is verified by the bank and no leverage beyond the exposure is created.

Currency swaps limited to the conversion of fixed-rate foreign currency debt into floating-rate KRW obligations, or vice versa, only where the notional principal corresponds to an existing cross-border loan or trade receivable, with evidence of cash-flow match and no speculative open position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment for the annual business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of the year following the fiscal year end, or within 3 months of the closing date for a non-calendar business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of the unpaid or underreported corporation tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent concealment, plus overdue interest and collection charges under the National Tax Collection Act; prolonged delinquency can trigger asset seizure, cancellation of business registration for a dormant entity, and judicial dissolution or strike-off under Commercial Act Article 176.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu local government through WETAX or local tax counter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from the fiscal year close, ordinarily 31 March for a calendar-year entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local tax of up to 20% of the unpaid surcharge, daily arrears interest under the Local Tax Collection Act, seizure of bank receivables, and administrative restrictions or cancellation of the business registration for continued nonpayment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT preliminary return and payment for January through June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 25 July immediately following the end of the first half, with payment due the same day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT Act penalties of up to 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing or underpayment, statutory arrears on unpaid VAT, and the ability of NTS to make a corrected assessment and attach assets; persistent non-filing may lead to business registration invalidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT final return and payment for July through December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 25 January following the end of the second half, with payment due the same day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT Act additional tax of up to 20% of the unpaid tax, arrears under the National Tax Collection Act, asset attachment, and administrative revocation of the business registration if the entity is deemed dormant or obstructs collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members meeting resolution approving financial statements and profit disposition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory records maintained at the registered office; no filing to the court registry unless registered matters are amended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year, or on the date fixed in the articles of incorporation if earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual members meeting exposes each responsible director to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act; repeated noncompliance may support an application for judicial dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and certified financial statements when the audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART for the audit report; National Tax Service receives the audited financial statements with the corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and financial statements approved by the members meeting before the corporate tax filing deadline, normally 31 March; the auditor files with FSS/DART within the periods prescribed by the Act on External Audit of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines against the representative and the audit firm, rejection of the corporate tax return if the required audit attachment is missing, regulatory sanctions by the Financial Services Commission, and possible adverse impact on the MFDS pharmaceutical wholesale license; direct strike-off is not automatic but may follow prolonged dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report and beneficial ownership update when foreign equity is 10% or more
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: KOTRA, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, or a State-designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any transfer of members equity, capital increase, capital reduction, liquidation event, or change in beneficial ownership; also on annual re-verification requested by the Korean bank under AML/KYC rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information; the company may lose foreign-invested company benefits and its bank may suspend or review high-risk pharmaceutical API trade payment rails such as letters of credit and bank wire transfers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Pharmaceutical wholesale distributor license maintenance and MFDS compliance notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and the local licensing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: License renewal every 3 years or as stated in the approval; any change in registered location, responsible pharmacist, or facility details must be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid pharmaceutical wholesale license is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a criminal fine of up to KRW 50 million under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; license cancellation by MFDS effectively ends the lawful business purpose and may trigger voluntary dissolution, judicial dissolution, or strike-off from the corporate register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Corporations, a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must obtain an independent certified CPA audit if its total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9 million. No separate private-LLC turnover or headcount threshold is imposed by that statute, but an audit can also become mandatory if the company belongs to a group required to prepare consolidated financial statements with total group assets of KRW 10 billion or more, if members holding at least 3% of voting equity request an audit, or if the Financial Services Commission designates the company as a public-interest entity under the External Audit Act. A pharmaceutical API wholesale company holding an MFDS license is not automatically required to file a CPA financial audit solely because of the license, but high-risk AML banking relationships frequently require a certified financial audit as a contractual condition for maintaining SWIFT LC and bank wire facilities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory audited entities apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) or Korean GAAP (K-GAAP for non-public entities), at the entity selection; unaudited Yuhan Hoesa entities must maintain double-entry accounting books consistent with K-GAAP and the Corporate Tax Act, and must prepare tax reconciliation schedules when submitting the annual corporate income tax return to NTS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain an annual public UBO filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa, but the company must keep the member register current and must file a foreign investment change report with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days of any transfer of equity or change in beneficial ownership when a foreign investor holds 10% or more of the total equity. The company must also cooperate with its Korean financial institution for annual customer due diligence and, for a high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale relationship, enhanced due diligence re-verification of all beneficial owners. Any membership transfer requires a written transfer agreement, an updated member register, transferor tax reporting, and, where applicable, the 30-day KOTRA/foreign exchange bank report.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 3,500 per year for registered office, resident agent, and professional Korean corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 45,000 per year for a mid-size Korean API wholesale entity subject to statutory audit, with the lower end applicable below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold or for a limited-scope K-GAAP engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national marginal corporate income tax rate (progressive schedule: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion). A local income tax surcharge of 10% of the national tax applies, producing a combined statutory top marginal burden of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory corporate income tax holiday for general wholesale API distribution. Available preferential items include research and development tax credits, facility investment tax credits, small and medium enterprise provisional income exemptions under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law, and Foreign Investment Promotion Act benefits such as cash grants and local tax reductions for qualified foreign investment in designated Free Economic Zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Corporate Income Tax Return (National Tax Service Form: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Calculation Statement) with attached supporting schedules such as financial statements, tax adjustment statements, and related-party transaction disclosures, submitted electronically through the HomeTax (NTS) electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory semi-annual interim prepayment obligations for corporations with prior-year tax liabilities; the annual return is filed once per fiscal year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year. For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following calendar year; if the deadline falls on a non-business day, it is extended to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number (Korean taxpayer identification number) assigned to the Yuhan Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident startup or foreign-owned branch must apply for a Korean business registration number with the competent District Tax Office before any filing; enter the assigned 10-digit number in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), net of discounts, returns, and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report on an accrual basis; include export sales and local sales. If a foreign head office arranges sales through the Korean entity, include the full invoice value and document the commission or agency role separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: purchase price of API inventory, inbound freight, insurance, customs duties, and directly attributable storage costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses that are ordinary and necessary for Korean operations are deductible. Cross-border purchases from foreign related parties must be evidenced by commercial invoices, customs declarations, and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit, calculated as Line 1a minus Line 1b.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compare the resulting gross margin to the comparable wholesale distribution margin; any abnormal deviation from arm's length indicates transfer pricing exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses (SG&A), including rental costs, employee salaries, regulatory license amortization, professional fees, and royalty expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident shareholders or foreign affiliates for royalties or services are deductible only if the expense is directly connected with the Korean business, is reasonable, and the recipient is the beneficial owner. Attach tax residence certificates and supporting service contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable business income before reconciliation: the net operating profit shown in the Korean GAAP financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Perform a full tax reconciliation by adding back non-deductible expenses and subtracting tax-exempt income. Non-resident companies are subject to the same Korean tax adjustment rules as domestic corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base and computed tax: application of progressive rates, foreign tax credits, and special income deductions or tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty foreign tax credits in the supplementary foreign tax credit schedule. Maintain all evidence of foreign taxes paid and proof of shareholding percentages and holding periods for any DTA relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party international transaction disclosure: aggregate amounts of cross-border sales, purchases, interest, royalties, and service fees paid to related foreign parties, with the transfer pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for any transaction with a foreign related party. Provide a description of each transaction, the functional and risk profile, and the arm's length price determination. Master File and Local File documents must be available upon NTS request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; unfaithful or fraudulent returns incur a 20% penalty on the underreported amount, while ordinary underreporting attracts a 10% penalty. Late payment surcharges accrue at 0.022% per day on outstanding taxes (approximately 8.03% per annum). Criminal prosecution for willful tax evasion may result in imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine not exceeding twice (aggravated cases up to five times) the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national dividend withholding tax, plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national withholding tax, resulting in an additional 2%, for a combined 22%) applied to dividends paid to non-resident shareholders of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced or zero dividend withholding rate under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority, and submit an 'Application for Reduction or Exemption of Non-Resident Withholding Tax' to the Korean NTS District Office before the dividend payment date. The beneficial owner must also complete an ownership statement demonstrating the shareholding percentage and minimum holding period required by the relevant treaty. If relief is not applied at source, a refund claim for over-withheld tax may be filed within 3 years from the statutory payment date. The Korean payor must retain the TRC, the approved application, and contracts evidencing beneficial ownership in its records.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding rates: royalties and license fees at 16.5% (15% national income tax plus 10% local surtax on the national tax, i.e., an additional 1.5%); interest payments at 16.5% on the gross amount (15% plus 1.5% local surcharge). Under tax treaties, rates are commonly reduced, with interest generally reduced to between 0% and 10% and royalties to between 5% and 15%, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to offshore financial centers, but applies an economic substance and substance-over-form doctrine through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in the Framework Act on National Taxes (Article 17) and the International Tax Adjustment Act (Articles 4 and 6). A Korean wholesale API distributor must demonstrate real business purpose and substance: physical premises, licensed pharmaceutical wholesale staff, actual purchase and sales contracts, inventory custody and risk-bearing, local management decisions, and independent financial capacity. A pure shell company or conduit lacking such substance may be recharacterized, its income attributed to the economic owner, and treaty benefits denied under the principal purpose test or limitation-on-benefits provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating API sales revenue, inflating cost of goods sold through fictitious invoices from related suppliers, or intentionally omitting export revenue from the Korean tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: National Tax Service reassessment with 20% additional tax for false returns on the underreported amount; late payment surcharges of 0.022% per day; criminal liability under the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 5 years for aggravated tax fraud or a fine not exceeding two times (serious cases up to five times) the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the statutory representative are jointly and severally liable for tax debts where corporate assets are dissipated or where the director personally directed the evasion; courts may impose travel bans, asset seizure in the director's name, and imprisonment in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling APIs at artificially low prices to a foreign related party in a low-tax jurisdiction, or inflating deductible royalties and management fees paid to a related entity, with no arm's length justification and no underlying economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority adjusts the transaction price to the arm's length amount, increases taxable income, imposes a 10% additional penalty for underreporting on the resulting deficiency, and may deny deduction of the overstated expenses; statutory interest and anti-abuse penalties also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve or sign false transfer pricing documentation face personal secondary liability when the company cannot pay the additional tax assessment; severe cases may lead to criminal liability for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse, and disguised profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring dividend distributions from the Korean LLC as tax-deductible royalties, service fees, or interest to a shareholder in a no-tax jurisdiction without actual technical services, loan funds, or business activity, or using the Korean entity as a shell for routing digital content and e-commerce sales profits out of Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the payment as a dividend, triggering 22% withholding tax; denial of DTA benefits under the principal purpose test; imposition of a 20% additional tax on unreported dividends; recovery of unpaid withholding tax with interest and penalties; possible criminal referral for willful tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are the ultimate beneficiaries of the recharacterized payments may be personally liable for the unpaid withholding taxes; the corporate veil may be pierced where the entity is used as a sham, subjecting directors to civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions, and pharmaceutical licensing violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Yuhan Hoesa as an intermediary to sell APIs to sanctioned entities, using split payments or countertrade to conceal transactions, failing to verify the ultimate beneficial owner, or operating wholesale distribution without the mandatory pharmaceutical wholesale license or required import/export permits under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Financial Transactions Reports Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act can lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to KRW 50 million; the competent pharmaceutical regulator may revoke the wholesale license and impose administrative monetary penalties; sanctioned business may be suspended and assets subject to freezing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal criminal fines and imprisonment, asset freezing, and debarment from licensed pharmaceutical activities; the limited liability shield is pierced where the company is a mere instrumentality of illegal conduct, exposing directors to civil damages and personal monetary penalties.
